text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Sweden plans to introduce some of the toughest laws in the world against child pornography - but not until the year 1999.
- Swedish fishery workers are being called in to work for Norway's salmon export industry which is facing a major recruitment problem. Young Norwegians do not want to work in fish factories.

- The result of a Nordic study -- the world's largest -- into a new potential AIDS vaccine came as a disappointment, says Britta Wahlen, who led the study at Sweden's Karolinska Institute. The vaccine had no discernible effect.
- Exports of oil from Denmark have risen to record levels over the past year and are helping to satisfy demand in Sweden, Norway and Germany.

- Swedish economists agree the central bank will link the crown to the Exchange Rate Mechanism but are divided on when. Some think nothing will happen until the Social Democrats party congress next September while others forecast it will happen before then.

- State-owned power company Vattenfall director Carl-Erik Nyquist says he is not interested in buying into Finnish counterparts. The Finnish government is planning to sell part of state-owned Imatran Voima Oy.
- The head of the Swedish Trade Union Confederation, Bertil Jonsson, says he is prepared to compromise with employers to develop a new wages and salary model before 1988 wage negotiations.
